samples.summary: Format-painter capture semantics changed, but the canonical subsystem doc was not updated
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:409-414` and :558-562 are the canonical description of `captureFormatAtCursor` ("bakes every boolean explicitly when copying… reading the *effective* value"). This change gives the painter two new documented-in-code behaviours: it strips the structural keys `image` / `pageNumber` / `href` from the buffer, and it now reads the format from the *first selected character* (`formatSourcePosition()`, selection start + 1) rather than the caret. Neither is recorded in that doc; only the roadmap table got a parenthetical ("shortcuts + toolbar toggle"). Per CONTRIBUTING the behaviour change should fold into the canonical doc rather than live only in code comments.

samples.summary: `Mod+Shift+C` no longer behaves exactly as before, contrary to the task's stated criterion
samples.evidence: The originating task (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md:33-34, and acceptance criterion :57) says the plan is to *lift* the keyboard-handler bodies and that "the shortcuts must keep behaving exactly as they do now". The lifted `copyFormat()` additionally changes what is picked up: `formatSourcePosition()` reads the selection's start+1 instead of `this.cursor.position`, so a backward drag now copies a different run than the shipped shortcut did. The structural-key strip is listed under "Review follow-ups" (:89-92); this selection-source change is not listed anywhere, so it is undeclared behaviour scope in a task that opens with "pure wiring: no new document behaviour".

samples.summary: Task doc cites a `NON_PAINTABLE_INLINE_KEYS` constant that does not exist in the implementation
samples.evidence: The todo's review follow-ups say "`NON_PAINTABLE_INLINE_KEYS` in `text-editor.ts` strips them", but the shipped code strips `image`/`pageNumber`/`href` by inline destructuring inside `captureFormatAtCursor` (text-editor.ts:3347-3352); grep for `NON_PAINTABLE_INLINE_KEYS` across packages returns nothing. Doc-to-implementation drift in the record of this change.

samples.summary: Dialog re-implements the orientation swap instead of reusing the exported `getEffectiveDimensions`
samples.evidence: `pageWidth`/`pageHeight` are computed by hand (`orientation === 'landscape' ? paperSize.height : paperSize.width`). `getEffectiveDimensions(setup)` in `packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:760` does exactly this and is exported from the package root (`packages/docs/src/index.ts:46`), and is what pagination / PDF export use. Two answers to the same question that can drift if the model ever grows a third orientation or a rotation flag.

samples.summary: cli.md's updated link row understates what the new gate drops (relative / scheme-less hrefs)
samples.evidence: The row now reads "an unsafe scheme (`javascript:`, `data:text/html`, …) drops the link and keeps the text", but `isSafeUrl` also rejects every scheme-less/relative href (see `packages/core/test/url.test.ts:19-21`, and the new test `packages/docs/test/serialize/markdown.test.ts` case `['a relative href', '/not/absolute']`). A document imported from HTML/DOCX with relative links will silently lose them in `wafflebase docs content --format md`, which the documented mapping does not say. The image row does state the equivalent rule; the link row should too.

samples.summary: Export-surface design doc still describes the docs Export dropdown as DOCX / PDF only
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/docs-pdf-export.md:503` documents `docs-export-button.tsx  # Export ▾ dropdown (DOCX / PDF)`; the menu now offers four formats and `safeFilename` accepts `md`/`txt`. No architectural change, so this is cosmetic doc staleness rather than a discipline breach.
